references.text: Isaiah 9:1-2 predicts that the people who walked in darkness will see a great light, a direct parallel image to Jesus' claim of coming as light to save from darkness.
Isaiah 42:6-7 describes the Messiah as a light for the nations to open the eyes of those sitting in darkness, which mirrors the purpose of Jesus' coming in John 12:46.
Isaiah 60:1-3 calls the people to arise and shine because the light is coming, and the nations will come to the light, a theme central to Jesus' self-understanding as the light of the world.
Psalm 27:1 expresses that the Lord is our light and salvation, a theological cornerstone that Jesus fulfills by identifying himself as the light that shines on the world.
In John 8:12, Jesus uses the same metaphor and promises that whoever follows him will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life, a direct echo of the statement in 12:46.
John 1:4-5 establishes that life was the light for people and that the light shines in the darkness, providing the theological context for Jesus' coming in chapter 12.
1 John 1:5-7 confirms that God is light and that fellowship with him requires walking in the light, not in darkness, linking faith to this light.
